controllingAuthority.summary: Police, court and other State or local records may be expunged on petition for the § 10-105(a) favorable dispositions. Absent a timely State's Attorney objection § 10-105(d)(2) directs the court to pass the order; Maryland appellate law holds a court has no discretion to deny where statutory entitlement is shown. As amended by the Expungement Reform Act of 2025, effective October 1, 2025.

exclusions: A PBJ entered on a charge under Transportation § 21-902(c), (d), (h) or (i), Criminal Law Title 2 Subtitle 5, or Criminal Law § 3-211, is not eligible at all under § 10-105(a)(3).

The § 10-105(a-1) carve-out for a pre-October 1, 2020 sodomy conviction or a pre-October 1, 2023 § 3-322 violation committed without consent, with a minor under 16, with a person the individual could not marry under Family Law § 2-202, or with a mentally incapacitated, physically helpless or substantially cognitively impaired individual.
Non-incarcerable vehicle-law and traffic violations, per the form's own affirmation.
The unit rule under § 10-107(b)(1), subject to the minor-traffic and cannabis-possession carve-outs in § 10-107(a).
Ineligible while a defendant in a pending criminal proceeding, § 10-105(e)(4)(iii).

For a PBJ, a conviction within 3 years of the PBJ other than a minor traffic violation or an act no longer a crime, § 10-105(e)(4)(i); extended to 15 years for a § 21-902(a) or (b) PBJ under § 10-105(e)(4)(ii).

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Conviction under Md. Code, Criminal Procedure § 10-110

controllingAuthority.summary: Convictions on the § 10-110(a) enumerated list may be expunged after the applicable period from completion of the sentence. Absent objection § 10-110(e)(3) makes the order mandatory. On a timely objection by the State's Attorney or a victim, § 10-110(f)(2) requires a hearing and five findings on the record. SB 432 (2025) overrode In re Expungement Petition of Abhishek I., so a probation violation no longer automatically disqualifies.

exclusions: Any conviction not on the § 10-110(a) enumerated list. Violent offenses, most serious felonies and registrable sex offenses are outside the list.
DUI and DWI convictions are not on the list; only a PBJ or other non-conviction outcome reaches the § 10-105 route.
Conviction of a new crime during the applicable waiting period, unless that new conviction is itself eligible for expungement, § 10-110(d).
Defendant in a pending criminal proceeding.
Unit rule under § 10-107, subject to the (a) carve-outs.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Shielding Under the Maryland Second Chance Act
tracks.publicName: Shielding a conviction from public view

controllingAuthority.summary: Twelve enumerated convictions may be shielded from public view three years after the sentence for all convictions for which shielding is requested is satisfied, including parole, probation or mandatory supervision. One shielding petition will be granted per lifetime, in one court in one county, and must include every eligible conviction from that court. Under § 10-305 a shielded conviction is not a conviction for the subsequent-conviction rule.

exclusions: Any conviction outside the twelve enumerated offences.
Domestically related convictions.
A pending criminal matter.
The unit rule.
A new conviction during the three-year window, unless that conviction is itself shieldable.
A second shielding petition. One will be granted, ever.

waitingPeriods.condition: Satisfaction of the sentence for all convictions for which shielding is requested, including parole, probation or mandatory supervision

The court notifies the Central Repository, custodians and the person, and under § 10-105.2 must notify the defendant of the right at disposition with a General Waiver and Release form.

exclusions: Cases where any charge resulted in a disposition other than the four qualifying outcomes.

tracks.legalName: Request to a Law Enforcement Unit for Expungement of a Pre-2007 Arrest Record, with District Court Application on Denial
tracks.publicName: Clearing police records from an arrest before October 2007

controllingAuthority.summary: For arrests, detentions or confinements occurring before October 1, 2007, the person requests expungement directly from the law enforcement unit within 8 years after the incident. The unit investigates and, if the facts are verified, expunges within 60 days. On written denial, or on failure to act within 60 days, the person may apply to the District Court with proper venue within 30 days of the denial, on DC-CR-071, which prints Rules Forms 4-503.3 and 4-503.4. The agency has 30 days after service to answer with specific grounds.

exclusions: Incidents occurring on or after October 1, 2007, which use the automatic police-record route.
Requests made more than 8 years after the incident. Because the incident must predate October 1, 2007, that window closed no later than October 2015.

waitingPeriods.condition: The incident, which must predate October 1, 2007
waitingPeriods.duration: The request must be made within 8 years of the incident. That window closed no later than October 2015.

destination.name: The law enforcement unit holding the record, then the District Court on denial
destination.detail: Stage 1 is an agency request; stage 2 is a District Court application on DC-CR-071. Neither stage is enterable, because the statutory 8-year request window has closed.

components.notes: Explains that the § 10-103 request window for a pre-October-2007 incident closed no later than October 2015, identifies DC-CR-071 as the Maryland District Court application form for the denial stage, and routes the participant to the automatic post-2007 route or the ordinary petition routes where those apply.

participantInputs.question: On what date did the arrest, detention or confinement happen?

selfHelpStopConditions: The 8-year request window has closed, which it has for every incident predating October 1, 2007.
A timely request was made and the agency answered with specific grounds, making the matter contested.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Not a legal-design gap. The mechanism, both stages and both instruments are fully known, and DC-CR-071 is in the corpus. The route is nonetheless not packet-capable for any participant, because § 10-103 requires the request within 8 years of an incident that must predate October 1, 2007, so the statutory entry window closed no later than October 2015. Retained as process_guidance on that ground: there is no participant who can still file, not an unresolved filing vehicle. Composed modelling was rejected because a composed route requires at least one available unit.

tracks.legalName: Expungement on Nolle Prosequi Before Service under § 10-104
tracks.publicName: Clearing a case the State dropped before you were ever served

controllingAuthority.summary: Where the State enters a nolle prosequi as to all charges in a District Court case with which the defendant has not been served, the District Court may order expungement of each court record, police record or other record the State or a political subdivision keeps as to the charges, unless the State objects and shows cause why the record should not be expunged. The District Court may not assess any costs against the defendant for a proceeding under this section.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Resolved from primary authority during this pass, closing the review's open item. Section 10-104 empowers the District Court to order expungement on the State's nolle prosequi entered before service, unless the State objects and shows cause, and bars any costs against the defendant. The statute describes court action on the State's disposition, not a participant petition, so no participant-facing filing exists. Retained as process_guidance on that ground rather than on the review's unresolved status.
